texts:
A support chat with a face is one script tag away. Concierge puts a rigged 3D avatar in the corner of your page. A visitor asks, the answer streams in, and the avatar starts speaking the first sentence while the rest is still arriving.

In the reel it is asked how to install itself, and it answers from the page it is sitting on.

When a visitor asks, the widget reads the live page (title, headings, nav and content) plus any facts you curate, and the answer streams back from a free-first inference chain, with failover across providers. Whatever your page says today is what it knows today.

three.ws/concierge

No account, no crawler setup, no per-seat pricing. The widget is open source, and you can add it as a script tag, a web component or an npm package.

Voice comes built in: push-to-talk speech input and browser-native speech output.

issues.quote: a script tag, a web component or an npm package
issues.problem: The passing check only confirms the page text 'Pick your flavor', which does not by itself enumerate the three install options. The reel's streamed answer does show a GitHub link to concierge-sdk, which supports 'open source' and the embed story, so the risk is low, but the enumerated list rests on thin evidence.
issues.fix: Optional: no change required since the check passed; if the page's 'Pick your flavor' section does not literally list script tag, web component and npm package, recapture that section of three.ws/concierge as evidence.

issues.problem: The final frame is visually identical to the 10.1 s frame, so the reel ends on a static beat rather than a resolving moment.
issues.fix: Optional: trim the reel to end as the answer finishes streaming, around 12 to 13 seconds.
